### ui/activity-feed.js
Filterable activity/event log table as an <activity-feed> custom element.
One element = one feed of timestamped, kinded events, presented with a
free-text query plus severity toggle chips (optionally family chips) with
live counts, a "showing N of M" readout and a clear-filter button.
Dependency-free; re-exports ui/activity-feed-math.js so one import serves
both.

IT IS A <data-table> UNDERNEATH (ui/data-table.js): rows, chips, counts,
the two empty states and the filter plumbing are that component's, and
this module supplies only what is feed-specific — three columns, the kind
badge, and the severity/family derivation. The public API below is
unchanged, including the persisted filter shape.

COLOR IS DERIVED, NEVER ENUMERATED: severity comes from the ACTION half of
a dotted kind ("manager.inbox_dropped" -> bad) and tints the badge pill;
family comes from the NAMESPACE half and picks a stable hue for the badge's
leading dot. A kind the producer adds tomorrow is styled the first time it
appears — a stylesheet enumerating known kinds drifts silently, and
everything unlisted shares one grey.

Entry text is rendered as TEXT NODES, never innerHTML, so producer strings
cannot inject markup; `messageRenderer` is the opt-in hook for richer
message DOM (the consumer owns that DOM's safety).

  <activity-feed empty-text="Nothing yet." storage-key="app.activity"
                 family-chips placeholder="filter activity...">
    <p>loading activity...</p>   <!-- light DOM: shown until upgrade -->
  </activity-feed>

Properties (all settable BEFORE the module loads — connectedCallback
performs the standard property upgrade, so a consumer script that ran first
never loses its values):
  entries: ActivityEntry[]        rows, rendered in the given order
  messageRenderer: (message, entry) => Node | string | null
  timeFormatter: (time, entry) => string   (default: locale date-time)
  familyAliases: Record<string,string>     e.g. {hooks: 'hook'}
  columns: Partial<ColumnLabels>           {time, kind, message} headings
  emptyText / storageKey / familyChips     mirror the attributes
  filter: StoredFilter                     get/set the whole filter
  clearFilter()                            drop query + every facet

Attributes: empty-text, storage-key (localStorage key for the filter;
unset = no persistence), family-chips (boolean), placeholder.

Event: `activity-filter-change` (bubbles, composed) — detail is the
StoredFilter; fired on every query/chip/clear change, never on data
changes.

Theme via --activity-* custom properties (activity-feed.css), which fall
back to generic --fg/--muted/--border/--panel/--accent plus
--failure/--running/--success/--skipped, so a host that already defines a
status palette needs no configuration.

Exports: class ActivityFeedElement, familyHue(family) -> number (0..359,
stable per name), types MessageRenderer, ColumnLabels — plus everything
from ui/activity-feed-math.js.

### ui/activity-feed-math.js
The feed's pure half. No DOM (unit-tested under node).

Exports:
  SEVERITIES — ['bad','warn','skip','good','info'], loudest-first (the
    chip order).
  SEVERITY_RULES — ordered [severity, RegExp] pairs matched against the
    action half, FIRST match wins. The order is load-bearing:
    'hook.disabled_rejected' must be bad (not warn on "disabled") and
    'reload.unverified' must be warn (not good on "verified").
  severityOf(kind) -> Severity — anything unclaimed is 'info' (ordinary
    lifecycle chatter). Degenerate kinds ('', no dot, undefined) -> 'info'.
  familyOf(kind, aliases?) -> string — the namespace half; `aliases` folds
    spellings ({hooks:'hook'}). Explicitly a map, not automatic plural
    stripping, which would turn the ordinary family 'status' into 'statu'.
  messageOf(entry) / timeOf(entry) — the message (accepts `message` or the
    `msg` alias) and epoch ms (NaN when absent/unparseable).
  matchesQuery(entry, query) -> boolean — case-insensitive over kind,
    message and field VALUES; whitespace-separated terms are ANDed.
  selectEntries(entries, filter?) -> FeedSelection — { shown,
    severityCounts, familyCounts, hiddenCount }. Counts cover the WHOLE
    input (a chip must keep showing what it hides) while `shown` is what
    survives every facet; input order is preserved.
  isFiltering(filter?) -> boolean — is the feed actually narrowed
    (whitespace-only queries are not).
  toStoredFilter(filter?) / parseStoredFilter(raw) -> StoredFilter —
    stable sorted {query, hiddenSeverities, hiddenFamilies} for
    persistence and the change event; parsing degrades to "no filter" on
    anything malformed rather than throwing.
  formatTimestamp(value) -> string — locale date-time; '' for a
    missing/unparseable time, so a row never shows "Invalid Date".

Types: ActivityEntry, Severity, FeedFilter, FeedSelection, StoredFilter

### ui/data-table.js
Declarative filterable/sortable table as a <data-table> custom element.
You declare columns and hand over rows; it owns the header and sort cycle,
the free-text query, the facet chip groups, the "showing N of M" readout
and the two distinct empty states. Dependency-free; re-exports
ui/data-table-math.js so one import serves both. <activity-feed> is built
on it -- nothing about tables is implemented twice.

VALUE vs RENDER vs TEXT is the column contract: `value` SORTS, `render`
DISPLAYS, `text` SEARCHES (defaulting to value's string). A duration column
sorts by milliseconds, shows "1.2s" and is searched as "1.2s"; collapse
them and the table sorts "10s" before "9s".

A `render` returning a string is appended as a TEXT NODE, never innerHTML,
so producer strings cannot inject markup. Returning a Node is the opt-in
for richer cells, and that DOM's safety is the consumer's.

  <data-table empty-text="No runs yet." storage-key="app.runs" searchable>
    <p>loading...</p>            <!-- light DOM: shown until upgrade -->
  </data-table>

Properties (all settable BEFORE the module loads -- connectedCallback
performs the standard property upgrade):
  columns: TableColumn[]     {key, label, value?, render?, text?, sortable?,
                              searchable?, align?: 'start'|'end', className?}
  rows: Row[]                rendered in the given order unless sorted
  facets: FacetGroup[]       {key, label?, of, order?, chipClass?,
                              decorate?, hidden?, local?, counts?, always?}
                             -- one chip row per group. local:false means
                             the HOST filters (server-side, before its own
                             row cap): chips still toggle/persist/emit but
                             the table drops nothing locally, and the group
                             MUST supply `counts` (its rows no longer
                             contain the hidden buckets, so derived counts
                             read x0 on exactly the chips needing a number).
                             Re-filtering a server-filtered window is how a
                             table empties itself and reports "nothing
                             matches" with the wanted rows just past the cap.
  sort: {key, dir} | null    null = the consumer's order
  rowClass / rowId           per-row class; stable id echoed in row-click
  searchText: (row)=>string  overrides what the query searches
  filteredEmptyText: (total)=>string   own noun for the filtered-empty state
  detailFor: (row)=>Node|Promise<Node>|null
                             per-row expandable detail; null = that row has
                             none. Requires rowId (expansion is tracked by
                             ID, so it survives the row objects being
                             replaced on every refresh). A Promise renders a
                             placeholder and paints when it resolves -- and
                             a rejection paints the error, because a row
                             that opens onto nothing looks broken. Rows with
                             a detail become disclosure controls
                             (aria-expanded, Enter/Space).
  expanded: string[]         the open rows' ids; assign to restore or
                             collapse ([] closes everything)
  toggleDetail(row)          open/close one row's detail
  styleText: string          extra CSS applied INSIDE the shadow root (the
                             escape hatch for styling rendered cells)
  emptyText / storageKey / searchable / placeholder   mirror the attributes
  filter: StoredTableFilter  get/set query + hidden buckets + sort
  clearFilter()              drop query + every hidden bucket (sort stays)

Attributes: empty-text, storage-key (localStorage key for query+chips+sort;
unset = no persistence), searchable (boolean), placeholder.

Events: `table-filter-change` (detail StoredTableFilter), `table-sort-change`
(detail SortState|null), `row-click` (detail {row, id}), `detail-toggle`
(detail {row, id, open}) -- all bubble and compose. Adding a `row-click` listener is also what makes rows INTERACTIVE:
they gain tabindex/role=button/Enter+Space and a focus ring. Derived from
the listener rather than a separate flag so "clicking a row does something"
and "a keyboard can reach a row" cannot be set inconsistently; a table with
no listener leaves its rows out of the tab order entirely.

Accessibility: headers carry scope=col and aria-sort, sortable headers are
focusable and activate on Enter/Space, and the "showing N of M" readout is
an aria-live=polite region so a query narrowing the table is announced.

Theme via --table-* custom properties (data-table.css), falling back to
generic --fg/--muted/--border/--panel/--accent.

Exports: class DataTableElement, types CellRenderer, TableColumn, FacetGroup
-- plus everything from ui/data-table-math.js.

### ui/data-table-math.js
The table's pure half. No DOM (unit-tested under node).

Exports:
  valueOf(row, col) / textOf(row, col) -- resolve a column's sort value and
    its searchable text.
  isBlank(v) -- null/undefined/'' -- the "absent" test the ordering uses.
  compareValues(a, b) -- numbers numerically, Dates chronologically, the
    rest as numeric-aware locale strings. BLANK ALWAYS SORTS LAST.
  sortRows(rows, columns, sort) -- STABLE copy; ties keep input order, and
    blanks stay last in BOTH directions (folding them into the signed
    compare is the classic bug: descending then answers a click with a
    screen of blank rows).
  nextSortState(current, key) -- the header cycle asc -> desc -> UNSORTED.
    Returning to unsorted is how the producer's order becomes reachable
    again; no asc/desc pair reproduces it.
  matchesQuery(haystack, query) -- every whitespace term must match (AND).
  selectRows(rows, columns, filter) -> {shown, facetCounts, total}. Facet
    counts cover EVERY supplied row, not the survivors: a chip reading "x0"
    the moment you hide its rows is exactly the number you needed in order
    to decide whether to unhide. Row order is preserved (sorting is a
    separate step).
  isFiltering(filter) -- is anything actually narrowed?
  toStoredTableFilter / parseStoredTableFilter / hiddenFromStored -- the
    persisted shape; parse degrades to "no filter" on anything malformed,
    so a stale localStorage value can never leave a table silently hiding
    rows.

NOTE the cap ordering this cannot fix for you: if the producer caps a page
BEFORE applying the same exclusions, a burst of unwanted rows fills the
page, this filter empties it, and the table reports "nothing here" while
the rows you want sit just past the window. Filter first, cap second, on
whichever side owns the data.

Types: DataRow (= object, NOT Record<string,unknown> -- a declared row
interface has no index signature), DataColumn, SortState, SortDir,
FacetGroupSpec, HiddenFacets, TableFilter, Selection, StoredTableFilter

### ui/canvas-text.js
Responsive multi-tier canvas text with alpha-fade truncation. A label is an
ordered list of TIERS, fullest → most compact; the largest tier that fits
the available width draws, and when even the last tier overflows it is
hard-clipped and its trailing ~2-3 characters fade to transparent — the
truncation signal — instead of an ellipsis (no width spent on '…', and the
final characters stay readable right up to the edge). Fitting is pure and
canvas-free: width comes from an injected MeasureText fn (cached char-width
arithmetic, or a memoized ctx.measureText) so callers control measurement
cost; only FadeTextPainter touches a canvas. Generic — no timeline types;
<timeline-view> drives its bar/gutter labels through it.

  deriveLabelTiers(label) → string[] — the full text; then a leading
    `owner/` path segment stripped (only when that segment contains no
    whitespace); then everything from the first ' - ' on stripped.
    Inapplicable tiers are skipped; always >= 1 tier.
    'wow-look-at-my/gosmopolitan - workflow_job' →
    ['wow-look-at-my/gosmopolitan - workflow_job',
     'gosmopolitan - workflow_job', 'gosmopolitan'].
  selectTier(tiers, availPx, measure) → index of the largest (earliest)
    non-empty tier that fits, or -1.
  clipToWidth(text, availPx, measure) → the longest prefix whose measured
    width fits ('' when none); measure must be monotonic over prefixes.
  fitTieredText(tiers, availPx, measure, opts?) → {text, tier, faded,
    width} | null — the fit decision: largest fitting tier (faded: false),
    else the most compact tier clipped to width (faded: true — draw with a
    fade tail), else null (suppress; a clip keeps at least
    opts.minClipChars ?? MIN_CLIP_CHARS (3) characters). `tiers` may be a
    plain string (a single tier).
  class FadeTextPainter — paint(ctx, text, x, y, width, fadePx, fill,
    halo?, haloWidth?) fills text (left-aligned; width = its measured
    width) with the last fadePx px alpha-fading to transparent, the
    optional halo stroked under the fill with the same fade; clear() drops
    cached gradients (call on theme changes). One cached gradient per
    (color, fade width) spans [0, fadePx] in user space and ctx.translate
    positions it per label — no per-label createLinearGradient, ever.
  FADE_TAIL_CHARS (2.5) — recommended fade width in character widths
    (fadePx = FADE_TAIL_CHARS * charW); MIN_CLIP_CHARS (3).

Types: MeasureText, FittedText, FitTieredOptions

### ui/combobox.js
Custom `<select>` dropdown replacement for browsers whose native dropdown is
broken or unusable — the motivating case is Tesla's in-car browser, which
renders the native dropdown in a separate OS window the page never captures, so
the option list is invisible. Replaces a `<select>` with an in-page popup
listbox built from ordinary DOM and appended to `<body>`, so no native dropdown
is ever opened. The original `<select>` stays in the DOM as the model: it is
hidden but keeps its value, and choosing an option sets that value and
dispatches `input` + `change`, so any existing listener (or framework, e.g.
lil-gui) runs unchanged. Options are read live at open time, so a select whose
`<option>`s are repopulated later keeps working. Keyboard: arrows/Home/End move,
Enter/Space choose, Escape close, type-ahead. Rendered in the light DOM; injects
its own themeable stylesheet once (compiled in — no CSS file to ship). No
dependencies. Re-exports everything from ui/combobox-logic.js so one import is
enough.

Importing the module auto-registers `<combo-box>` (unless that tag is taken).

  import { installSelectFallback } from '.../ui/combobox.js';
  installSelectFallback();              // Tesla UA by default; { force: true } for any browser

  import '.../ui/combobox.js';          // registers <combo-box>
  //  <combo-box><select>…</select></combo-box>

Activation (installSelectFallback / shouldEnable): the UA gate matches Tesla by
default; override with `match: (ua) => boolean`, bypass with `force: true`, or
force at runtime via `?combobox=force`, `localStorage['js-combobox']='force'`,
or `globalThis.__JS_COMBOBOX_FORCE__ = true`.

Exports:
  installSelectFallback(opts?) → () => void
    Upgrade all current <select>s and (unless observe:false) watch for new ones
    via a MutationObserver. No-op unless shouldEnable(opts) passes. Returns a
    disposer that stops observing. Opts: force, match, root (ParentNode,
    default document), observe (default true), existingTrigger.
  upgradeSelect(select, opts?) → void
    Upgrade one <select>. Idempotent; skips multi-selects. opts.existingTrigger
    (select) => HTMLElement|null lets you reuse a host's own trigger that
    already paints the value (e.g. a lil-gui .widget whose .display stays in
    sync) instead of generating one.
  upgradeAll(root?, opts?) → void
    Upgrade every <select> under root (default document).
  openPopup(select, trigger, syncLabel?) → void
    Open the popup for a (hidden) select anchored to a trigger element.
  closePopup() → void
    Close the open popup, if any (one is open at a time).
  injectStyles() → void
    Inject the component stylesheet once (idempotent; no-op without a DOM).
    Called automatically by upgradeSelect.
  COMBOBOX_CSS: string
    The stylesheet source. Theme by overriding the --cb-* custom properties
    (--cb-bg, --cb-fg, --cb-border, --cb-accent, --cb-radius, --cb-popup-bg,
    --cb-popup-fg, --cb-popup-border, --cb-active).
  class ComboBox extends HTMLElement
    Backs <combo-box>; upgrades its child <select> on connect (no UA gate).
    Exported so you can register under another name.
  Plus everything re-exported from ui/combobox-logic.js (shouldEnable and the
  other pure helpers below).

Types: UpgradeOptions, FallbackOptions (extends EnableOptions + UpgradeOptions
with root?: ParentNode, observe?: boolean).

### ui/combobox-logic.js
The combobox's pure logic. No DOM or browser APIs (unit-tested under node);
ui/combobox.js is the DOM-bound half that consumes it.

Exports:
  shouldEnable(opts?: EnableOptions) → boolean
    Whether the fallback should activate: true if opts.force, the UA matches
    (opts.match, default isBrokenDropdownUA), or a manual override is set
    (?combobox=force, localStorage['js-combobox']='force', or
    globalThis.__JS_COMBOBOX_FORCE__ = true). Reads only guarded globals, so
    it is safe (and false by default) outside a browser.
  isBrokenDropdownUA(ua) → boolean
    The default UA gate: /Tesla|QtCarBrowser/i.
  hasForceParam(search) → boolean
    Whether a location.search-style string carries combobox=force.
  optionText(opt) → string
    An option's display text: textContent, else value, else ''. Structural —
    takes a real HTMLOptionElement or any { textContent?, value? }.
  firstEnabledIndex(options) / lastEnabledIndex(options) → number
    First/last non-disabled index (0 / length-1 fallback when none).
  stepActiveIndex(current, dir, options) → number
    Next active index stepping ±1 with wrap-around, skipping disabled
    options; all-disabled or empty lists leave `current` unchanged.
  typeAheadTarget(buffer, activeIndex, options) → number
    First enabled option whose text starts with buffer (case-insensitive),
    searching forward with wrap-around — a fresh single-character buffer
    starts after the active option (repeats walk the matches), a longer
    buffer includes it; -1 when nothing matches.
  computePopupPlacement({trigger, viewport, popup}) → PopupPlacement
    Fixed-position placement for a popup anchored to a trigger rect: prefers
    below, flips above when below can't fit the (320px-capped) height and
    above is roomier; maxHeight fits the chosen side within [80, 320];
    minWidth = trigger width, maxWidth = min(max(width, 200), viewport - 16);
    left keeps a 4px viewport inset. Returns {top, left, maxHeight, minWidth,
    maxWidth, openUp}.

Types: EnableOptions {force?, match?}, OptionLike {text, disabled?},
PlacementInput, PopupPlacement

### ui/markdown.js
Markdown -> DOM renderer for untrusted prose (a PR description, an issue
body, a comment). Parsing is micromark via mdast-util-from-markdown with GFM
on, so coverage is real CommonMark + tables, task lists, strikethrough and
literal autolinks — nested lists nest, a destination with balanced parens
survives whole. Rendering builds elements with createElement/createTextNode
and textContent only.

There is NO HTML string anywhere in the pipeline: source -> mdast -> DOM. So
there is also no innerHTML and no sanitizer to configure — the usual "render
to HTML, then scrub the HTML" round trip, and every mis-scrub bug that comes
with it, does not exist here. Safety instead lives in ui/markdown-parse.js's
sanitizeTree, which runs on the tree before any node reaches this walker:
raw HTML becomes literal text, and unsafe link/image URLs lose their link.
This module is therefore mechanical — it maps node types to elements and
cannot reintroduce either problem.

Images render as their alt text linked to the source, NOT loaded, because
fetching a remote image named by untrusted markdown leaks the reader's IP and
referrer to whoever wrote it; opt in with renderImages for markdown you
trust. Re-exports everything from ui/markdown-parse.js so one import is
enough.

Cost: the micromark/mdast payload is ~37 KB gzipped, code-split into its own
chunk that only these two modules import — nothing else in the library pays
for it. Want different output (a framework's virtual DOM, linked #123
references, custom table markup)? Walk parseMarkdown()'s mdast tree yourself
rather than post-processing these elements.

  import { renderMarkdown } from '.../ui/markdown.js';
  const el = renderMarkdown(pr.body, { headingOffset: 2 });
  if (el) host.appendChild(el);   // null === nothing to show

Exports:
  renderMarkdown(source, options?: RenderMarkdownOptions) → HTMLElement | null
    A fresh container div, or null when source is absent/empty/whitespace —
    so a caller can tell "no content" from "content that rendered to
    nothing" and show its own empty state.

Elements produced: p, h1-h6, ul/ol/li (ordered lists carry `start` when it
  is not 1), blockquote, pre>code (code[data-lang] when the fence names a
  language), strong, em, del, a, img (only with renderImages), hr, br,
  table>thead/tbody>tr>th/td (cells carry style.textAlign from the column
  alignment), and a disabled checkbox input for a GFM task item.
  Footnotes and link definitions render nothing.

Options (RenderMarkdownOptions), all optional:
  classPrefix (default 'md') — root class, plus <prefix>-code on the code
    block's <pre>, <prefix>-task on a task checkbox, <prefix>-table on a
    table. Nothing else is classed; style by element.
  headingOffset (default 0) — added to every heading level, clamped to
    h1..h6. Pass a positive offset when the page owns its own headings: a
    description's '# Title' is a section of that description and should not
    outrank the page's real heading.
  linkTarget (default '_blank', null for same-tab) — when set, rel is
    'noopener noreferrer' too; never hand an untrusted link a live opener.
  renderImages (default false) — emit real <img> instead of a link.
  document (default globalThis.document) — render into another document.

### ui/markdown-parse.js
The renderer's pure half: markdown text -> a SAFE mdast tree. No DOM
(unit-tested under node). Parsing is micromark's job; this module's job is
the step after, and it is the safety boundary — everything it guarantees
holds for ui/markdown.js's output too, because the walker only ever sees a
sanitized tree.

Two things make untrusted markdown dangerous, and both are closed in the
tree: CommonMark says `<script>alert(1)</script>` in the source IS html (and
mdast faithfully reports an `html` node), and `[x](javascript:alert(1))` is a
perfectly well-formed link whose danger is entirely its URL.

Exports:
  parseMarkdown(source) → Root | null
    A GFM mdast Root, already sanitized. null for absent/empty/whitespace-
    only input, or a tree with no content.
  sanitizeTree(tree) → Root
    Rewrites in place; idempotent. `html` nodes become `text` nodes carrying
    the same characters (nothing is dropped — the reader sees exactly what
    the author typed, as text). link/image URLs go through safeHref: a
    refused link is REPLACED BY ITS OWN CHILDREN, so its visible label
    survives unlinked, and a refused image becomes its alt text. Reference-
    style links/images whose definition is refused are flattened the same
    way — the destination lives in a separate node, so a check that only
    looked at `link` nodes would miss them entirely.
  safeHref(raw) → string | null
    The href to use, or null if it must not become a link. Absolute URLs
    only on http/https/mailto; relative URLs (including protocol-relative
    '//host/path') have no scheme of their own and pass through. Scheme
    detection is the URL parser's, not a string match, so the usual evasions
    are already handled: it lowercases the scheme and strips leading
    whitespace and embedded tab/newline/CR, making 'JaVaScRiPt:',
    ' javascript:' and 'java<TAB>script:' all resolve to javascript: and be
    refused.
  markdownToText(source) → string
    Plain-text flattening for a tooltip or one-line summary: markup removed,
    block-level nodes newline-separated. Pure — no DOM.

Types: re-exports mdast's Root, Nodes, RootContent.

### ui/perf-graph.js
Compact, stackable, canvas-rendered performance graph as a <perf-graph>
custom element. One element = one scrolling metric strip (frame time, fps,
heap, any numeric gauge): push(value) appends a sample, the newest sample
hugs the right edge, history scrolls left. Every pixel — including all text
(label, current value, avg/min/max readout, tick labels) — is drawn on one
shadow-DOM <canvas> via fillText: zero DOM text nodes, no layout, no
dependencies. Redraws only when new data / size / theme arrive (dirty flag,
at most one rAF pending, none when idle) and skips drawing entirely while
the tab is hidden or the element is scrolled out of view (one deferred draw
on becoming visible). DPR-aware backing store (crisp on HiDPI); when
samples outnumber plot pixels the trace switches from a polyline (+ soft
area fill) to per-pixel min-max columns via binMinMax. Steady-state draws
allocate nothing. Re-exports everything from ui/perf-graph-math.js so one
import is enough.

Importing the module auto-registers <perf-graph> (unless that tag is taken).

  import '.../ui/perf-graph.js';

  <perf-graph label="frame" unit="ms" budget="16.7"></perf-graph>

Element <perf-graph> attributes (all optional; properties mirror them, and
property setters reflect back to the attributes):
  label   — name drawn top-left
  unit    — 'ms' (default) | 'fps' | any custom suffix | '' for bare numbers
  history — samples kept/displayed (default 240); changing it live preserves
            the newest samples
  height  — element height in CSS px (default 48; compact)
  min/max — fixed scale ends; omit either for autoscale (autoRange + nice
            1-2-5 gridlines, range quantized so ticks stay put)
  budget  — guide value (e.g. 16.7) drawn as a dashed amber line, always
            kept inside the displayed range

Element properties / methods:
  push(value: number)  — append one sample; schedules (at most) one rAF redraw
  clear()              — drop all samples
  refreshTheme()       — re-read the --perf-graph-* custom properties
  label, unit, history, height: reflected properties for the attributes
  min, max, budget: number | null (null = attribute absent)

CSS custom properties (read via getComputedStyle, cached; dark Scratch
Proto defaults — set on the element, an ancestor, or :root):
  --perf-graph-bg        — background            (#0d0f14)
  --perf-graph-line      — trace / columns       (#00e47a)
  --perf-graph-fill      — area fill under the polyline; 'none' disables
                           (rgba(0, 228, 122, 0.10))
  --perf-graph-grid      — gridlines             (rgba(200, 205, 216, 0.08))
  --perf-graph-text      — label/stats/ticks     (#6b7280)
  --perf-graph-value     — current-value readout (#e8ecf4)
  --perf-graph-budget    — budget line           (#f0a500)
  --perf-graph-font      — canvas font family    ('JetBrains Mono', 'SF Mono',
                           'Cascadia Code', 'Fira Code', monospace)
  --perf-graph-font-size — base font size in px  (10)

Stacked HUD example — several graphs sit flush in a plain column (:host is
display:block, width:100%, margin-free), all fed from one rAF loop:

  <div id="hud" style="position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; width: 260px;">
    <perf-graph id="ft"  label="frame" unit="ms"  budget="16.7"></perf-graph>
    <perf-graph id="fps" label="fps"   unit="fps" min="0" max="120"></perf-graph>
    <perf-graph id="mem" label="heap"  unit="MB"  history="600" height="32"></perf-graph>
  </div>

  import '.../ui/perf-graph.js';
  const ft = document.getElementById('ft');
  const fps = document.getElementById('fps');
  const mem = document.getElementById('mem');
  let last = performance.now();
  requestAnimationFrame(function tick(now) {
    const dt = now - last;
    last = now;
    ft.push(dt);
    fps.push(1000 / dt);
    if (performance.memory) mem.push(performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize / 2 ** 20);
    requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  });

Exports:
  class PerfGraphElement extends HTMLElement
    Exported so you can register under another name:
    customElements.define('my-graph', PerfGraphElement)
  THEME_DEFAULTS — the default theme values keyed like the CSS properties
  Plus everything re-exported from ui/perf-graph-math.js.

### ui/perf-graph-math.js
The graph's pure math. No DOM or browser APIs (unit-tested under node);
hot paths are allocation-free — the ring allocates only on construction /
setCapacity, and computeStats/binMinMax fill caller-owned outputs.

Exports:
  class SampleRing
    Fixed-capacity float32 ring buffer: constructor(capacity), push(v),
    at(i) (0 = oldest; NaN out of range), latest() (NaN when empty),
    clear(), setCapacity(n) (preserves the newest samples), getters
    length / capacity. Capacity clamps to >= 1.
  computeStats(ring, out: PerfStats) → PerfStats
    Fills the caller-owned { current, avg, min, max } (returns it).
    Non-finite samples are skipped for avg/min/max; all fields NaN when
    empty; current is the raw latest sample.
  autoRange(dataMin, dataMax, opts?: AutoRangeOptions) → DisplayRange
    Padded display range { min, max }. opts: fixedMin/fixedMax pin an end
    exactly, pad (default 0.1) pads each free end by pad × span,
    includeZero extends a free end to 0 (a zero floor from non-negative
    data is not padded below 0). Degenerate-safe: empty/flat data still
    yields a usable nonzero span.
  niceStep(span, maxTicks) → number
    Smallest 1-2-5 × 10^k step splitting span into <= maxTicks intervals.
  niceTicks(lo, hi, maxTicks) → number[]
    Tick positions on that grid within [lo, hi] (at most maxTicks + 1;
    [] for an invalid range). Allocates — call only when the range moves.
  binMinMax(ring, bins, outMin: Float32Array, outMax: Float32Array) → number
    Min-max downsample for more-samples-than-pixels: sample i lands in bin
    floor(i * bins / count), so every finite sample influences exactly one
    bin and outMin[b] <= outMax[b]. Empty bins are NaN; bins clamps to the
    out arrays; returns the number of non-empty bins.
  formatValue(v, unit) → string
    Deterministic readout formatting: non-finite → '—'; 'ms' → adaptive
    decimals (|v| >= 100 → 0, >= 10 → 1, else 2) + 'ms'; 'fps' → rounded +
    'fps'; other non-empty unit → 1 decimal + suffix; '' → bare adaptive
    number.

Types: PerfStats, AutoRangeOptions, DisplayRange

### ui/timeline-view.js
Canvas-rendered realtime swimlane timeline as a <timeline-view> custom
element. A shared horizontal time axis across the full width; stacked
labeled lanes (left gutter; labels too wide for it clip with a fade-out
tail — see ui/canvas-text.js — full text via tooltip;
lane order = exactly the order supplied — never re-sorted internally),
each a band of interval bars (left = start, right = end). A lane grows
extra sub-tracks when intervals VISIBLE in the current window overlap,
and rows are VERTICALLY STICKY (a stateful per-lane TrackAllocator): an
interval KEEPS its row while it stays on screen — panning and live
updates never reshuffle the rows being watched — an interval scrolling
out and back gets its old row back when still free (bounded LRU row
memory; the memory survives setData, so a live resync leaves rows put),
and new arrivals take the lowest conflict-free row, so lane height
recovers from the bottom once a tall burst scrolls away (never by
re-rowing what is still visible); a historical parallelism burst stops
padding its lane once it scrolls out of view, a lane with nothing
visible collapses to one track, and height changes ease over ~150ms
(snapped under prefers-reduced-motion; hit-testing tracks the animating
layout). AUTO-FIT (default on; opt out
with the no-auto-fit attribute): when the natural stack — every lane at
--timeline-track-height — would overflow the host's height, whole lanes
are demoted to the compact track height (--timeline-track-height-compact,
default 4 CSS px; the canvas' DPR scaling supplies device pixels) one at
a time, tallest (most parallel) lane first — ties demote the LOWER lane
first, so top-of-chart lanes keep detail longest — until the stack fits
or every lane is compact (only then does vertical lane scrolling engage,
as before). Demotion is immediate; re-promotion needs ~10% height
headroom (hysteresis — heights can't flap at the boundary); the demotion
set re-derives from the visible window each pass (a parallelism burst
scrolling away hands its demotion to the now-tallest lane,
deterministically); and demotion/promotion rides the same ~150ms height
tween. Compact slivers stay legible: bars keep the 2px minimum width and
a border capped to the sliver, pips shrink but never below a 4px-tall
diamond, in-bar labels are suppressed below fit height, and gutter labels
degrade gracefully (full → smaller/faded → skipped below ~10px lane
height, where the gutter tooltip still names the lane) without ever
overlapping a neighbor. Read fitState / listen for 'fitchange' to observe
the demotion set. Everything is data — lanes,
intervals, optional connectors between intervals, vertical time markers;
dynamic lane count (1-50+), smooth with thousands of in-window intervals
(viewport culling, dirty-flag rAF drawing, DPR-aware backing store capped
at 3, adaptive idle pacing — full rate while interacting + a ~500ms
grace, ~30fps idle, ~10fps idle on battery via navigator.getBattery
feature-detection, paused while the document is hidden — and those tier
rates are a CEILING: while the only motion is clock-driven (the
follow-now scroll, ongoing-bar growth) the effective rate is
min(tier fps, device px per second) — the rAF loop keeps running and
skips frames that would be pixel-identical, on an even frame-aligned
cadence (clockDrawBudgetMs; never timer wakes, so motion stays smooth
at every zoom, and at normal zooms the px rate meets the tier so pacing
is exactly the tier's) — and a chart with nothing animating draws
nothing at all; input/data/hover changes still render immediately via
the dirty flag). Canvas text is
kept crisp: the 2d context is OPAQUE (alpha: false — the chart paints
its own background every frame, and an opaque canvas gets subpixel text
antialiasing where an alpha one gets grayscale-only; keep --timeline-bg
an opaque color), and every TEXT draw origin snaps to the device-pixel
grid (labels step in whole pixels while lanes tween/scroll — deliberate;
grid-aligned glyphs beat smeared ones). Rendering is
stability-first: the viewport origin is snapped to whole DEVICE pixels
once per frame and nothing else on the time axis is rounded (text
origins are the one per-element exception — nothing tiles against a
label), so follow-mode scrolling translates the whole scene in integer
device-pixel steps and bars never jiggle relative to each other. The now
line is the one VIEWPORT-anchored element: its x is computed from the
RAW view (nowLineX) — never the snapped render view, whose per-frame
quantization error used to wiggle the line between adjacent device
pixels — so while follow-now is engaged it holds perfectly still as the
scene scrolls under it. Hatch/stipple pattern fills are phase-anchored
to the CONTENT they fill (a span's unclamped origin, a coverage gap's
start), not to the canvas, so the texture travels 1:1 with its span
instead of the span sliding over a static screen-space pattern. Not a
Gantt (many bars per row), not a flame chart (no nesting).

Color encodes CATEGORY: interval.category (default lane.group, then
laneId) hashes to a stable hue — same category = same color, forever —
with a small deterministic tone offset so near hues still separate.
Rendering STYLE encodes state/phase via a named style map: interval.state
and segment.kind look up a treatment {pattern solid|hatch|stipple|outline,
alphaScale, saturationScale, lightnessScale, border {width, dash,
emphasis}, glyph none|bang|dot, dimmed}. Built-ins: '' solid; 'emphasis'/'failed'
unmissable (2px emphasis border + corner bang glyph + stipple — hue
untouched); 'dim'/'queued' translucent + desaturated; 'hatch'/'waiting'
45-degree stripes; 'outline' hollow; 'cancelled' hollow + DASHED
category-hue border — unmissably "stopped, not failed" at any zoom: never
the emphasis color, never the bang, never a solid success body (a BAR's
border dash falls back to solid below ~12px width, where dashes read as
broken corners — the hollow body still separates a tiny cancelled bar
from a solid one; this solid-below-legibility rule applies to any dashed
border style on bars. Instant PIPS are exempt: a cancelled pip keeps its
dashed diamond outline — the declared pattern is rescaled so 3-5 whole
dash cycles close around the perimeter — so a cancelled instant carries
the same dashed signature as a cancelled span). A style with `dimmed: true`
(the dim/queued/hatch/waiting built-ins) renders as ONE uniform filter
over the region's GEOMETRY: fill, hatching, and border all get the same
dimColor transform (50% saturation, 50% value — hue and alpha
untouched), so the section reads quieter than a running span. Label and
badge text is deliberately EXEMPT from that filter: every span-surface
label (bar labels, adapter-composed badge strings
like queue ordinals) always renders at the full-contrast foreground
(--timeline-fg) over a thin counter-color halo (labelHaloColor: dark
rim under a light fg, light rim under a dark one), so text stays
readable over solid, dimmed, hatched, and mixed surfaces at EVERY zoom
— deriving text color from the section underneath produced unreadable
grey-on-grey labels that flipped with the zoom level as the label's
anchor crossed segment boundaries. Ongoing intervals (end == null)
render to the live now edge with a subtly pulsing leading edge (static
under prefers-reduced-motion; while the feed is STALE they freeze at the
last vouched timestamp and restyle dim + hatched — see Feed staleness
below). Zero/near-zero-DURATION intervals (mapped
width under ~3px at the current zoom) render as instant diamond pips at
their start time — clearly distinct from bars, still category-colored,
state-styled (a failed instant gets the thick emphasis border + stem),
hoverable and clickable via a widened hit target. The
bar-vs-pip decision comes from the DURATION mapped through the scale
(durationWidthPx) — translation-invariant, so shapes never flicker while
the timeline scrolls — and a real-duration bar is clamped to MIN_BAR_PX
(2px), never demoted to a pip.

Instant markers CLUSTER at scale: pips whose centers would visually
overlap in the current window (within ~12px of a neighbor — a greedy
transitive sweep, re-derived per layout pass) merge into ONE point-like
STACKED marker — the SAME diamond pip as a single instant, drawn as a
stack of exactly THREE copies (two ghost copies offset straight RIGHT
behind the true front pip with a depth fade — front full-bright, middle
dimmer, back dimmest; always three, NEVER scaled by the member count —
the stack silhouette alone says "several live here", and there is no
count text on the canvas: the tooltip carries the real ×N count;
membership is exactly "would visually overlap", so a stacked pip can
only ever BE a cluster) — never a duration bar: an instantaneous event
has no length, and neither does a pile of them. The cluster packs
as ONE row slot spanning its member extent, so a burst of coincident
instants can't blow up the lane height; membership depends only on time
deltas and the scale, so panning never re-clusters (no jitter — the
marker sits at the member extent's midpoint, sliding along the visible
slice at a window edge instead of hiding off-screen), while ZOOMING IN
progressively splits every cluster until each pip stands at its true
timestamp. A cluster is also capped at CLUSTER_MAX_SPAN_PX (24) wide,
so no pip is compacted more than ~12px from where it belongs and a
densely populated track keeps rendering as a row of markers however far
you zoom out — it never chains into a single marker at the midpoint. A cluster styles by its members' shared state where uniform
(an all-'dim' cluster stays dim-flavored; mixed states fall back to the
neutral default) and hits as {type: 'cluster', intervals, lane}:
hovering shows a COMPONENT-BUILT summary tooltip (count, time extent,
up to 8 member labels then '+K more', a zoom hint) — tooltipFor is
never consulted for clusters — and clicking ZOOMS to the member extent
(centered, ~60% fill, min-span floored) so the cluster splits, instead
of dispatching intervalclick; fully coincident members zoom to the
minimum span and stay one marker (they genuinely share a timestamp —
the tooltip lists them). Ongoing intervals and real-duration bars never
cluster. Single pips keep exact tooltipFor/intervalclick behavior.

Spans CLIPPED by the viewport carry an
edge-continuation cue: the clipped end darkens into a SHADOW over the
last ~12px toward that edge — black at the edge itself, clearly darker
than the background, easing to clear inward, plus a 1px near-black
boundary line — so the span reads as sliding UNDER the window edge,
which covers it and casts a shadow on it (never a fade to the
background: that made the span look like it evaporates there). Applies
left when the true start is scrolled off-screen, right when the true
end — or an ongoing bar's extent in a parked view — exceeds the window,
over every treatment (solid, hollow, hatched, terminal cuts). Spans
whose edge coincides with the window edge are exempt (they genuinely
start/end there), as are stubs too short to reach through the shadow
zone (which would swallow them). Bar labels are RESPONSIVE MULTI-TIER
text (ui/canvas-text.js): each label is an ordered list of fallbacks,
fullest → most compact — explicit via the interval's labelTiers, else
derived from `label` (leading `owner/` segment stripped, then the
trailing ' - suffix') — and the widest tier that fits the bar draws.
When even the most compact tier overflows, it hard-clips and its last
~2-3 characters alpha-fade to transparent (never an ellipsis — no width
spent on '…', and the characters stay readable up to the edge); below a
3-character clip the label is suppressed — it never spills into
neighboring bars — and labels stick to the plot edge while a bar's start
is scrolled off-screen (just past the continuation shadow when one is
active).

A MINIMAP strip (32px, its own canvas) runs along the bottom while data
exists: the FULL loaded extent — earliest loaded interval widened by
coverage knowledge (first covered time, the exhausted-history boundary)
through max(now, latest end) — as per-lane collapsed density marks in
category hues at low alpha (no text; sub-pixel runs stay ≥1px so piles
read as density), a now tick (muted while stale), and the current
viewport as a brighter window rect with grabbable LEFT/RIGHT handles.
Dragging a handle adjusts that window edge live (clamped to the extent
and the ~2s..~7d span limits; dragging one handle past the other CLAMPS
at the minimum span, never flips); dragging the middle pans the window
at constant width (1:1 under the pointer, clamped inside the extent);
clicking the strip outside the window centers the window there and
continues as a grab. Handle hit zones are generous (~8px, reaching
outside the rect but shrinking inside so even a narrow window keeps a
grabbable middle; the window rect itself never draws under ~6px).
Minimap gestures go through the SAME view semantics as canvas gestures:
a middle/right-handle drag is pan-like (backward disengages follow;
docking at the live edge re-engages), the left handle is zoom-like (a
pinned live edge stays pinned), and moving into uncovered past fires
loadRange exactly like panning there. The strip repaints only when the
main chart draws (same rAF loop, same idle pacing). It hides — ceding
its band back to the plot — when there is no data, when the host is
shorter than ~140px, or with the no-minimap attribute; the plot canvas,
lane packing, auto-fit, tooltip clamps, and hit-testing all size against
the remaining plot area automatically, and the corner buttons ride up
above the strip. Fullscreen and the minimap compose (the strip stays at
the bottom of the filled viewport).

Importing the module auto-registers <timeline-view> (unless the tag is
taken).

  import '.../ui/timeline-view.js';

  <timeline-view id="tl" style="height: 400px"></timeline-view>

  const tl = document.getElementById('tl');
  const now = Date.now();
  tl.setData({
    lanes: [
      { id: 'build-queue', label: 'build queue' },
      { id: 'deploy-queue', label: 'deploy queue', group: 'deploys' },
    ],
    intervals: [
      { id: 'j1', laneId: 'build-queue', start: now - 300_000, end: now - 120_000,
        label: 'job #17', category: 'build',
        segments: [{ start: now - 300_000, end: now - 240_000, kind: 'queued' }] },
      { id: 'j2', laneId: 'build-queue', start: now - 100_000, end: now - 100_000,
        label: 'skipped', category: 'build', state: 'dim' },     // instant pip
      { id: 'j3', laneId: 'deploy-queue', start: now - 90_000, end: null,
        label: 'deploy #4', category: 'deploy' },                 // ongoing
      { id: 'j4', laneId: 'deploy-queue', start: now - 200_000, end: now - 150_000,
        label: 'deploy #3', category: 'deploy', state: 'failed' },
    ],
    connectors: [{ fromIntervalId: 'j1', toIntervalId: 'j3', label: 'triggers' }],
    markers: [{ time: now - 150_000, label: 'config change', kind: 'emphasis' }],
    coverage: { start: now - 300_000, end: now },
  });
  tl.loadRange = async (start, end) => {
    const rows = await fetch(`/api/history?from=${start}&to=${end}`).then(r => r.json());
    tl.mergeData({ intervals: rows });
    return { exhausted: rows.length === 0 };
  };
  tl.addEventListener('intervalclick', (e) => showDetails(e.detail.interval));

Element <timeline-view> — data API (properties/methods, never attributes):
  setData({lanes?, intervals?, connectors?, markers?, coverage?})
    Replace all data. coverage: {start, end} declares the time range the
    supplied intervals fully cover (async-history bookkeeping).
  mergeData(data)   — merge into the current set: lanes/intervals dedupe by
    id (intervals replace in place), connectors by (from, to, kind),
    markers by (time, label, kind). How loadRange results are supplied.
    Re-layout is COALESCED to one rAF (like drawing): a burst of merges —
    or a backlog flushed on tab wake — costs one O(N) rebuild per frame,
    not one per call, so it's safe to hammer without freezing the page.
  setLanes(lanes) / setIntervals(intervals) / setConnectors(connectors) /
  setMarkers(markers) — replace one slice of the data.
  clear()           — drop everything.
  markFresh(ts?)    — stamp the live feed fresh without merging data
                      (setData/mergeData stamp automatically; see Feed
                      staleness below).
  staleAfterMs      — staleness threshold (see Feed staleness below).
  styles            — StyleMap spread over the built-ins (see above).
  legendEntries     — TimelineLegendEntry[] {glyph, text}: consumer rows
                      appended under the built-in vocabulary in the "?"
                      legend panel — how a consumer explains glyphs it
                      composes into LABELS (queue-position badges like
                      '⧗ group · 3rd', holder counts like '⏳N'). Copied
                      on set; an open panel re-renders immediately.
  colorFor          — (interval, lane) => cssColor | null override.
  tooltipFor        — (hit: TimelineHit) => string | Node | null; null/
                      undefined hides. Default tooltip shows label,
                      category, state, the HOVERED phase segment (a
                      'segment: <kind> · <duration>' line — named by its
                      style-map kind, the legend's vocabulary, so no
                      legend round-trip to decode a stripe), start/end,
                      duration, segment durations. An interval hit
                      carries that hovered phase as `segment`
                      (SegmentHit {index, kind, start, end} — clamped ms
                      window; null over the base bar) — an ADDITIVE
                      field, so existing callbacks keep working and opt
                      in by reading `hit.segment`.
                      Node content is appended, never innerHTML.
                      Long lines WRAP inside the box (unbroken tokens like
                      run ids/error blobs included; newlines in string
                      content are honored), and pathological content clips
                      at a max height instead of outgrowing the host —
                      nothing ever spills past the tooltip border. NEVER
                      called for cluster hits — their summary tooltip
                      is component-built (see instant clustering above).
  loadRange         — (start, end) => Promise<{exhausted?: boolean} | void>.
                      Invoked (one request at a time, min-chunk widened;
                      a rejected load is retried on a fixed ~2s cadence
                      forever — no growing backoff, no attempt cap, no
                      give-up, and the uncovered hatching stays visible
                      while it keeps trying) when the viewport reaches
                      uncovered past. BACKWARD history only: requests
                      never reach past the covered end, so the sliver
                      between the last covered time and the live "now" is
                      never asked for — keep coverage.end current via
                      setData/mergeData `coverage` on every live update
                      (a live feed owns the forward edge; loadRange can
                      then never chase the advancing clock and refire per
                      round-trip). With no coverage at all, one bootstrap
                      request may reach "now" and latches once settled.
                      Uncovered regions draw hatched (with 'loading…'
                      while in flight) — visually distinct from
                      covered-but-empty; {exhausted: true} pins a dashed
                      'history ends here' boundary with a darkened void
                      before it and stops further requests.
  nowProvider       — () => msSinceEpoch override for replay/testing.
  fitState          — read-only {enabled: boolean, demoted: laneId[]}:
                      the current auto-fit demotion set in display order
                      (mirrors the latest 'fitchange' event).

Interval shape: {id, laneId, start, end?, label?, labelTiers?, category?,
state?, segments?, data?}. start/end are ms since epoch or Date; end null/
undefined = ongoing. labelTiers: ordered label fallbacks, fullest → most
compact (overrides the tiers derived from label; label — else
labelTiers[0] — stays the tooltip/full text). segments: [{start, end?, kind}] phases WITHIN the
bar, each styled via kind (e.g. a dim leading 'queued' phase, a hatched
'waiting' span); end null = to the bar's end. A segment whose kind
resolves to the 'outline' pattern is a TERMINAL CUT (e.g. a kill tail:
cancel requested → finished): it renders as a dark scrim over the dead
tail — plus, once the tail is >= ~4px wide, a cut line in the segment's
own hue (the cancelled border's color family) marking the kill point;
hairline tails stay scrim-only, because a lone line flush against the
span's end border reads as a stray artifact — and NEVER vanishes: it
keeps a >= 3-device-px footprint (grown backward from its end) at any
zoom, unlike decorative phases, which skip below half a pixel. data is
opaque and echoed back in events/tooltips. Connector: {fromIntervalId, toIntervalId, kind?,
label?} — a muted S-curve between two bars, endpoint-dotted, highlighted
on hover; if one endpoint id is missing from the data a dashed stub +
open circle marks it and the tooltip says which side isn't loaded.
Marker: {time, label?, kind?} — dashed vertical line; kind 'emphasis'
renders in the emphasis color.

Viewport / follow:
  viewport          — getter {start, end} (ms).
  DEFAULT window    — until the first user gesture or setViewport call,
                      the visible span is ASPECT-DERIVED: 3 minutes at a
                      16:9 container, scaled linearly by the host's
                      actual aspect ratio (defaultSpanForAspect, clamped
                      ~2s..~7d), ending at now — and re-derived on every
                      host resize, END anchored, while still untouched.
                      Any gesture or setViewport latches the window as
                      CHOSEN and the default never applies again;
                      followNow / jumpToNow move position only and do
                      NOT latch. Consumers that call setViewport keep
                      their own initial window entirely.
  setViewport(start, end) — explicit window (span clamped ~2s..~7d;
                      hard-stops at now; engages follow only when it
                      ends within the 2-device-px snap zone of now;
                      latches the window as chosen — see DEFAULT window).
  fitToInterval(id, {pad?}) — fit the viewport to ONE interval: its span
                      full-width plus `pad` fraction each side (default
                      0.05) — the run-detail-dialog convenience (an
                      embedded instance shows just the clicked span with
                      no viewport math). A thin setViewport wrapper:
                      counts as a consumer-chosen window (latches),
                      clamps + now-stops the same; instants/sub-~2s
                      spans center in the minimum window. Returns false
                      (viewport untouched) for an unknown id.
  followNow         — boolean (default true): right edge pinned to live
                      now. Any backward PAN (wheel, drag, arrow keys)
                      disengages immediately — even a tiny step, so
                      trackpad panning escapes the pin. ZOOMS never
                      inherit the pin: the anchor is ALWAYS the gesture's
                      focal point (cursor / pinch midpoint / keyboard
                      center), even while following — during the gesture
                      the timestamp under the cursor stays under the
                      cursor, and the zoomed view re-earns follow by the
                      same snap rule as any fresh gesture (zooming AT the
                      live edge keeps following; an anchored zoom-in away
                      from it parks, and follow re-docks magnetically on
                      a later gesture). One deliberate asymmetry: a
                      zoom-out pinned at the live edge can't show the
                      future, so the end stop caps it right-anchored —
                      the same clamp a parked zoom-out hits at the stop.
                      User-driven views HARD-STOP at
                      now (every pan/zoom/pinch/keyboard/setViewport
                      clamps the right edge there), and a gesture parking
                      the right edge within 2 DEVICE pixels of that end
                      stop re-engages follow — dragging to the stop
                      re-docks reliably, while a view parked merely NEAR
                      the edge (3+ device px) stays put. The small follow
                      lead (FOLLOW_LEAD_FRAC = 2% of span ahead of the
                      now line) is EASED, never assigned: engaging keeps
                      the view exactly where the gesture parked and
                      glides the lead in over ~200ms; disengaging lets
                      the backward deltas consume the lead, any residual
                      gliding out the same way — the view never teleports
                      in a single frame (prefers-reduced-motion snaps
                      instead).
  jumpToNow()       — re-engage follow, keeping the span: a fast ~250ms
                      glide from wherever the view is to the followed
                      position, never a teleport (reduced motion snaps).
                      Under maxTime it parks the view at that stop
                      instead — the same "take me to the end" gesture.
  minTime           — number|Date|null (default null): the earliest time
                      the view may scroll back to. Every gesture, jump
                      and default-span re-derivation stops there, the
                      minimap extent starts there, the zoom-out ceiling
                      becomes the bounded range (with maxTime), and
                      loadRange is never probed for a range before it —
                      set it to the first timestamp you can serve.
  maxTime           — number|Date|null (default null): the latest time
                      the view may reach. INDEPENDENT of minTime: either
                      side can be set alone. Setting it stops the forward
                      scroll — this instant REPLACES the clock as the
                      live edge, so the right stop, ongoing (end = null)
                      bar ends and hit tests read it, and follow mode,
                      the now line, the jump-to-now pill and feed
                      staleness all switch off. That is what makes a
                      chart of finished content static: nothing moves
                      without a gesture, and the render loop idles.
                      Setting it while following glides the follow lead
                      out rather than teleporting the view.
  fullscreen        — boolean property, reflected as the `fullscreen`
                      attribute: viewport-fill mode. The host goes
                      position:fixed inset:0 over the whole viewport
                      (deliberately NOT the Fullscreen API — no permission
                      prompt; the :host([fullscreen]) rules are !important
                      so they beat page styles sizing the host), the page
                      scroll locks while active (html overflow hidden,
                      previous value restored — the page's scroll offset
                      survives the round trip exactly), and everything
                      re-derives through the normal resize path (the DPR
                      cap stays at 3). Escape exits (handled only while
                      fullscreen — never swallowed otherwise). A corner
                      ⤢/⤡ toggle button sits at bottom-right, visible in
                      BOTH follow and parked modes (the jump-to-live pill
                      slides in to its left); hide the button with the
                      no-fullscreen-button attribute (the property and
                      attribute keep working programmatically).
  Events: 'viewportchange' {start, end, followNow} on user-driven changes,
  'intervalclick' {interval, lane} (single intervals only — a cluster
  click zooms to its member extent instead), 'intervalhover'
  {interval|null, lane|null}, 'connectorclick' {connector}, 'laneclick'
  {lane} (a click on a gutter label — lets consumers make lanes
  navigable), 'fitchange' {demoted: laneId[]} whenever auto-fit's
  demotion set changes, 'stalechange' {stale, lastFresh} on
  feed-staleness transitions, 'fullscreenchange' {fullscreen} on
  viewport-fill transitions.
  A built-in jump-to-live pill appears while not following (hide it with
  the no-live-pill attribute).

Legend (the "?" pill): a small button stacked above the fullscreen
  toggle opens an in-place glyph dictionary — the component-owned
  vocabulary (filled/hollow instant pips, the stacked cluster pip, the
  failed stipple + bang, hatched wait/queued phases, dim de-emphasis,
  the cancelled span's dashed hollow + terminal kill cut) followed by
  any consumer `legendEntries`. Rows name a GLYPH and its meaning —
  nothing meta — and cover only glyphs that are actually cryptic:
  self-explanatory chrome (the minimap, edge treatments) stays out.
  Pure DOM chrome in the shadow root: it works in fullscreen, costs the
  canvas render path nothing (rows build only when the panel opens),
  swatches are CSS-drawn in a neutral hue (they teach shape, not any
  category color), Escape or any chart gesture closes it (inside
  fullscreen, Escape closes the panel first, then the mode), and the
  no-legend attribute hides the pill entirely.

Feed staleness (a dead live feed is impossible to misread):
  Every setData/mergeData stamps the feed FRESH; markFresh(ts?) stamps
  explicitly — call it from polls that returned "no changes" so a
  quiet-but-healthy feed never reads as stale. When staleAfterMs (default
  10_000; tune to ~2 poll intervals; 0 or a non-finite value disables —
  use that for static, loaded-once datasets) passes without a stamp the
  chart goes STALE instead of extrapolating dead data: the live edge —
  ongoing (end=null) bar ends, the now line, the follow pin, the forward
  clamp on user views — FREEZES at the last vouched timestamp (a finished
  5s run whose end never arrived shows ~5s, never "running forever"),
  ongoing bars restyle as unknown (dimmed + hatch overlay, no pulse), the
  now line goes muted + dashed, a built-in "live data stale (Ns) —
  reconnecting…" note counts up forever (fixed cadence, never gives up),
  and 'stalechange' {stale: true, lastFresh} fires. A followed view stops
  scrolling (the frozen content never slides out of view). The next
  stamp exits stale mode and the live edge GLIDES back to the real clock
  (~250ms; composes with the follow pin — no teleport on recovery either;
  reduced motion snaps). On 'stalechange' back to fresh, consumers should
  do ONE full resync (setData) before resuming incremental merges — runs
  that ended during the outage otherwise stay unknown; a full setData
  mid-stale is handled gracefully and recovers in the same call.
  staleState — read-back getter {stale, lastFresh}.

Attributes (scalar toggles only): no-live-pill, no-auto-fit (disable
compact-lane auto-fit — every lane keeps the full track height),
history-end-text (boundary label, default 'history ends here'),
empty-text (empty-state hint), fullscreen (reflected viewport-fill mode
— see the fullscreen property), no-fullscreen-button (hide the corner
fullscreen toggle), no-minimap (hide the bottom minimap strip),
no-legend (hide the "?" legend pill).

Interaction: plain wheel / two-finger scroll routes by DOMINANT axis
with a GESTURE-LEVEL AXIS LOCK (WheelGestureRouter): the FIRST decisive
unmodified event classifies the stream — horizontal-dominant
(|deltaX| > |deltaY|) locks 'h', vertical-dominant (ties included)
locks 'v' — and that lock governs every unmodified event arriving
within WHEEL_GESTURE_GAP_MS (200ms) of the previous one (a real swipe
is a stream whose jittery minority events are individually
opposite-dominant; per-event routing leaked them). An 'h' gesture is
consumed WHOLE: deltaX pans time and the minor vertical component
nudges the lane stack when it overflows the host — it never creeps the
page. A 'v' gesture follows the NESTED-SCROLLER contract, latching its
target from the lane stack's scrollability at lock time: while the
stack can move in the wheel's direction the whole gesture SCROLLS THE
STACK in place (consumed, clamped at its edges — browser-style scroll
latching; drag and arrow keys still scroll it too), and when it cannot
— already at that edge, or no overflow — NOTHING is consumed for the
gesture (no preventDefault, no zoom: the page scrolls normally over
the chart, its horizontal jitter never pans the chart sideways), so
the page is always reachable past a tall chart. A
DECISIVE opposite-axis event mid-gesture — beating the locked axis by
more than WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_RATIO (2x) with at least
WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_MIN_PX (24px) — re-locks on the spot (proportional
jitter can never clear both thresholds; a genuine direction change, or
a chart freshly scrolled under the cursor mid-page-scroll that
mis-locked on a jitter event, recovers within one tick). A
FRESH/ISOLATED event routes exactly by the per-event dominant-axis
table; all deltas deltaMode-normalized;
ctrl/meta+wheel zooms anchored under the cursor (pixel-precise trackpad
deltas apply 1:1; discrete wheel steps glide ~130ms; always consumed —
never browser page-zoom; the cursor anchor holds while follow-now is
engaged too — see followNow); shift+wheel pans time; pointer drag pans
both axes (pointer capture); two-pointer pinch zooms anchored at the
pinch midpoint (also while following); keyboard when focused
(tabindex 0): arrows pan (shift = faster), +/- zoom, End = jump to now,
Home = jump to the earliest known data. The wheel listener sits on the
HOST, so those rules apply over the DOM chrome (live pill, fullscreen
toggle, stale note) exactly as over the canvas — a horizontal delta is
consumed wherever it lands — and the host + canvas carry
overscroll-behavior-x: none (HORIZONTAL only), so pulling further at
the left pan boundary never chains into the browser's
history-back/forward navigation gesture, wheel or touch, while the
VERTICAL axis stays free to chain page scrolling exactly like the wheel
router promises. TOUCH mirrors the same rule via the plot canvas'
touch-action: pan-y: a one-finger vertical swipe scrolls the PAGE (the
browser claims it and the element stops), a horizontal one-finger drag
pans the chart, and two-finger pinch-zoom still belongs to the element
(pan-y doesn't allow browser pinch) — the accepted tradeoff is that
one-finger vertical LANE-drag is gone on touch (arrow keys and desktop
drag are unaffected); the minimap strip keeps touch-action: none (a
pure horizontal-drag control), and chrome buttons keep touch-action:
manipulation so taps stay instant. Page-LEVEL containment (html/body)
stays the embedding page's own business.

CSS custom properties (dark Scratch Proto defaults; see THEME_DEFAULTS):
  --timeline-bg            — plot background          (#0d0f14)
                             (must be OPAQUE — the canvas is opaque for
                             subpixel text AA, so a translucent bg would
                             composite on black, not on the host)
  --timeline-fg            — bar labels / primary     (#e8ecf4)
  --timeline-muted         — axis/lane labels         (#6b7280)
  --timeline-grid          — vertical time gridlines  (rgba(200,205,216,0.07))
  --timeline-hairline      — lane separators          (rgba(200,205,216,0.10))
  --timeline-row-tint      — alternating lane tint    (rgba(255,255,255,0.015))
  --timeline-now           — now line + live pill     (#00e47a)
  --timeline-emphasis      — failed/emphasis accents  (#ff5c5c)
  --timeline-stale         — stale-feed note          (#f0a500)
  --timeline-font          — canvas + chrome font     (JetBrains Mono stack)
  --timeline-font-size     — base font size px        (11)
  --timeline-cat-lightness — category oklch L 0..1    (0.62)
  --timeline-cat-chroma    — category oklch chroma    (0.11)
  --timeline-track-height  — sub-track height px      (18, clamped 10..40)
  --timeline-track-height-compact — auto-fit demoted sub-track height px
                             (4, clamped 2..track-height; CSS px — DPR
                             scaling supplies device pixels)
  --timeline-gutter-width  — lane gutter px           (0 = auto-size)
  --timeline-tooltip-bg / --timeline-tooltip-fg — tooltip chrome.
  Category colors use oklch when supported (hsl fallback). refreshTheme()
  re-reads the properties after retheming.

Exports:
  class TimelineViewElement extends HTMLElement
  THEME_DEFAULTS — default theme values keyed like the CSS properties
  Types: TimelineData, TimelineHit, LoadRangeFn, TooltipFn, ColorFn,
    TimelineLegendEntry {glyph, text}
  Plus everything re-exported from ui/timeline-view-math.js.

### ui/timeline-wire.js
A compact COLUMNAR wire format for feeding <timeline-view> a lot of events,
plus the frame-paced driver that decodes one without blocking the page. Use
it when a feed is big enough that JSON stops being free. Measured on 100k
events: 7.5 B/event gzipped against JSON's 28, and ~5x less main-thread time
to decode, because nothing parses per record and no per-row object is built
until something asks for one.

It decodes a LAYOUT, not a vocabulary — it has no idea what your events mean.
Turning columns into intervals (labels, states, lanes) is your domain logic
and stays in your code. The column NAMES are yours too, declared in a schema
you pass in, which is what lets one format serve different producers.

  interface WireSchema {
    magic: string;              // 4 chars, checked against the payload
    deltaU: readonly string[];  // ascending unsigned, delta-encoded (ids)
    deltaZ: readonly string[];  // signed, zigzag delta-encoded (epoch ms)
    plain:  readonly string[];  // plain unsigned, one per row
    bits:   readonly string[];  // one bit per row
    strings: readonly string[]; // dictionary-encoded + one index per row
  }

  interface Columns {
    n: number;
    u: Record<string, Float64Array>;   // delta-decoded unsigned
    z: Record<string, Float64Array>;   // delta-decoded signed (epoch ms)
    p: Record<string, Int32Array>;     // plain unsigned
    b: Record<string, Uint8Array>;     // bitsets — read with bitAt()
    s: Record<string, StringColumn>;   // dictionaries — read with stringAt()
  }

  interface DecodedPage { c: Columns; maxId: number;
                          retentionStart: number; now: number }

Exports:
  decodePage(buf: Uint8Array, schema: WireSchema): DecodedPage
  decodePageGen(buf, schema): Task<DecodedPage>   // yields between chunks
  runSliced<T>(task: Task<T>, onSlice?: (ms: number) => void): Promise<T>
  nextFrame(): Promise<void>
  drain<T>(task: Task<T>): T
  stringAt(c, name, i): string
  bitAt(c, name, i): boolean
  rowOfId(c, idColumn, id): number      // binary search, -1 if absent
  rowObject(c, i): Record<string, string | number | boolean>
  CHUNK_MS, STEP
  types: WireSchema, Columns, StringColumn, DecodedPage, Task

THE LAYOUT (v1), in order: 4-byte magic, maxId (uvarint), retentionStart
(varint, epoch ms), now (varint, epoch ms), n (uvarint), then the numeric
columns, the bitsets (ceil(n/8) bytes each), and the string columns
(dictionary, then one index per row) — each in schema order. A string column
whose dictionary holds exactly ONE entry carries no index run at all (it was
unused in this window) and reads as that entry for every row. A change to the
layout is a NEW VERSION, new magic — never an edit to this one.

Decoding throws on bad magic, a truncated payload, or TRAILING BYTES: a
payload that does not decode exactly did not decode. Trailing bytes usually
mean your schema disagrees with the producer's column list.

PACING — the part that matters for a big page. runSliced runs ONE CHUNK PER
FRAME, where a chunk is a FRAME'S WORTH of work (CHUNK_MS): it claims a frame,
then pulls generator steps ACROSS phase boundaries until the budget is spent.
One unit per frame means the unit's cost IS the frame's load. Defining a chunk
as one step of one phase instead took 70 frames to do 8 ms of work; filling
the frame took it to 3. A frame is a global TURN, so two concurrent loads get
different frames rather than sharing one, and it is claimed BEFORE the work —
yielding afterwards leaves seams where two flows both run unwaited.

Intervals should carry the page's Columns as their shared payload — ONE
reference, not a per-row object — and recover the row on hover with
rowOfId(). At 100k events the per-row objects are enough allocation to cause
GC pauses inside decode chunks (measured 4-7 ms), which is exactly what the
frame budget exists to avoid.

  import { decodePageGen, runSliced, stringAt, rowOfId }
    from '.../ui/timeline-wire.js';

  const SCHEMA = {
    magic: 'TLC1',
    deltaU: ['id'], deltaZ: ['start'], plain: ['dur', 'status'],
    bits: [], strings: ['lane', 'kind', 'label'],
  };

  const res = await fetch('/feed', { headers: { Accept: MY_MEDIA_TYPE } });
  const buf = new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer());
  const { c, maxId } = await runSliced(decodePageGen(buf, SCHEMA));

  // columns -> your intervals (your domain logic, chunked however you like)
  const intervals = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < c.n; i++) {
    intervals.push({
      id: String(c.u.id[i]),
      laneId: stringAt(c, 'lane', i),
      start: c.z.start[i],
      end: c.z.start[i] + c.p.dur[i],
      label: stringAt(c, 'label', i),
      data: c,                       // ONE shared reference for the page
    });
  }

THE ENCODER lives here too, in Go — `github.com/wow-look-at-my/js-snippets/
timelinewire` (a nested module in this repo). Import it rather than writing a
second encoder; that is what the format used to drift over. It is the same
schema-driven shape (Schema/Page/Encode, plus Decode so a Go producer can read
its own payload), and one fixture,
timelinewire/testdata/golden-v1.b64, is written by its test and decoded by
this module's, so neither half can move alone.

### ui/timeline-view-math.js
The timeline's pure math. No DOM or browser APIs (unit-tested under
node); ui/timeline-view.js is the canvas-bound half that consumes it.

Exports:
  Data types: TimelineLane {id, label, group?}, TimelineInterval,
    TimelineSegment {start, end?, kind}, TimelineConnector,
    TimelineMarker {time, label?, kind?}, TimeView {start, end},
    TimeRange {start, end}, IntervalStyle, StyleMap, StylePattern,
    PackItem, LaneMetrics, LaneLayout, HitRect, SegmentHit,
    CategoryColorOptions, CoverageOptions.
  toMs(t: number | Date) → number
  Scale/zoom: timeToX(t, view, width), xToTime(x, view, width),
    panView(view, dt), zoomView(view, anchor, factor, minSpan?, maxSpan?)
    (anchor-preserving, span clamped; MIN_SPAN_MS = 2s, MAX_SPAN_MS = 7d),
    fitSpanView(start, end, pad?, minSpan?) → TimeView (one span plus
    pad fraction — default 0.05 — each side; a padded window under
    minSpan centers the span instead — the element's fitToInterval),
    defaultSpanForAspect(hostW, hostH, refSpanMs?) → span ms (the
    aspect-scaled DEFAULT window: DEFAULT_SPAN_REF_MS = 3 min at 16:9,
    linear in the container aspect, clamped to the span limits;
    degenerate sizes fall back to the reference),
    wheelDeltaToPixels(delta, deltaMode, lineHeight?, pageHeight?)
    (deltaMode 0/1/2 → px), zoomFactorForWheel(deltaPx) (exponential,
    composable; ZOOM_PX_PER_DOUBLE px per doubling),
    routeWheel(WheelInput, lanes: LaneScrollInput) → WheelRoute {zoomPx,
    panPx, laneScrollPx, consumed} (the PER-EVENT router — exact for a
    fresh/isolated event: ctrl/meta = zoom, always consumed; shift =
    time pan; else the DOMINANT axis decides — horizontal-dominant
    (|dx| > |dy|) pans time, consumed, with the minor deltaY nudging
    lanes only when they overflow; vertical-dominant incl. ties follows
    the nested-scroller rule with the direction-aware LaneScrollable
    {up, down} form — consumed with laneScrollPx = dy exactly while the
    stack can move in dy's direction, else routes NOWHERE — and with the
    legacy boolean overflow form NEVER consumes vertical wheels;
    consumed=false means DO NOT preventDefault, let the page scroll;
    deltaMode normalized), interface LaneScrollable {up, down} + type
    LaneScrollInput = boolean | LaneScrollable,
    classifyWheel(WheelInput) → WheelClass 'zoom' | 'pan' |
    'passthrough' (the per-event routing decision without magnitudes,
    normalized the same way; the lanes input deliberately has no input
    here — a test-pinned invariant guarantees routeWheel(e, o).consumed
    === (classifyWheel(e) !== 'passthrough') for every no-headroom o:
    the boolean form and {up:false, down:false}),
    class WheelGestureRouter — route(WheelInput, lanes, ts) →
    WheelRoute (the STREAM-level router the element feeds every wheel
    event through: the first decisive unmodified event locks the
    gesture's axis — 'h' consumes every unmodified event, dx pans /
    overflow-gated dy lane-scrolls; 'v' latches lane-vs-page from the
    stack's scrollability at lock time and holds it for the gesture
    (lane: every event consumed as laneScrollPx, edges clamped by the
    element; page: nothing consumed — always the verdict for boolean
    lanes input) — until
    unmodified events pause longer than the gap, or a mid-gesture event
    beats the locked axis by more than WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_RATIO with at
    least WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_MIN_PX and re-locks on the spot; ts is the
    caller's clock (e.timeStamp), never Date.now(); a FRESH router
    equals routeWheel on any single event — test-pinned; modifier
    events delegate to routeWheel and neither read nor extend the lock;
    zero-delta unmodified ticks are inert),
    WHEEL_GESTURE_GAP_MS (200 — unmodified-wheel silence that ends a
    gesture), WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_RATIO (2), WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_MIN_PX (24 —
    the decisive-flip thresholds, both required, on normalized pixels),
    clampViewToNow(view, now) → TimeView (the hard right
    end stop: a user view's end never passes now, span preserved),
    TimeBounds {min: number|null, max: number|null} (static scroll
    bounds; each side independent, null = unbounded),
    clampViewToBounds(view, bounds) → TimeView (clamp into the bounds,
    span preserved: past max shifts back, before min shifts forward; a
    span wider than the range collapses onto [min, max] exactly;
    null/non-finite sides are ignored),
    boundedMaxSpan(bounds, maxSpan?, minSpan?) → number (the zoom-out
    ceiling: the range when both sides are set, else maxSpan; never
    below minSpan),
    followAfterGesture(wasFollowing, prevEnd, next, now, isPan,
    msPerDevicePx) → boolean (the follow rule: a backward pan always
    disengages; while already following anything else stays pinned —
    zooming at the live edge keeps following; while not following,
    re-engage only when the right edge lands within
    FOLLOW_SNAP_DEVICE_PX (2) DEVICE pixels of the now end stop — pass
    span / (plotWidthCss * dpr); FOLLOW_LEAD_FRAC is the pinned lead),
    followLeadAt(fromFrac, targetFrac, elapsedMs, tweenMs) → number (the
    eased follow lead, fractions of span: easeOutQuad, monotone, no
    overshoot, per-tick step bounded by |target-from|*2*dt/tween, lands
    exactly on the target at elapsed >= tween; tweenMs <= 0 snaps — the
    reduced-motion path; FOLLOW_LEAD_TWEEN_MS (200) eases
    engage/disengage, JUMP_TO_NOW_TWEEN_MS (250) the jump/pill glide and
    the stale<->fresh live-edge transition),
    gestureLeadFrac(endMs, now, span, maxFrac) → number (the lead a
