    gesture legitimately holds: (end-now)/span capped at maxFrac — a
    gesture consumes lead, never mints it; seeds both lead easings),
    snapViewToDevicePixels(view, plotWidthCss, dpr) →
    TimeView (origin snapped to whole device pixels, span preserved —
    the single global rounding that makes scrolling translate the scene
    in integer device-pixel steps), snapTextOrigin(v, dpr) → number (a
    CSS-px coordinate snapped to the nearest whole device pixel — for
    TEXT draw origins only, where per-element rounding is crispness, not
    jiggle; never round bar geometry per element),
    nowLineX(now, view, gutterX, plotWidthCss, dpr) → number (the now
    line's snapped x, computed against the RAW view — while follow-now
    pins the view the result is frame-to-frame CONSTANT; the snapped
    render view's per-frame quantization error would wiggle it between
    adjacent device pixels — landing on the half-device-px grid for a
    crisp 1px stroke; the one viewport-anchored exception to the global
    rounding policy).
  Staleness: STALE_AFTER_DEFAULT_MS (10_000), feedIsStale(now,
    lastFresh, staleAfterMs) → boolean (never stale before any data or
    with a non-finite/non-positive threshold; strictly-past-threshold
    trigger), liveEdgeTarget(now, lastFresh, staleAfterMs) → number (the
    live edge all live semantics advance to: now while fresh, FROZEN at
    lastFresh once stale — ongoing bars never extrapolate a dead feed).
  Time ticks: TIME_TICK_STEPS (the 1/2/5/10/15/30 ladder ms→s→min→h→d),
    timeTickStep(span, maxTicks), timeTicks(view, maxTicks, tzOffsetMs?)
    (aligned to round local times; pass -new Date().getTimezoneOffset() *
    60000), formatTimeTick(t, step, tzOffsetMs?) (granularity follows the
    step; local-midnight ticks label as the date), formatTimeFull(t,
    tzOffsetMs?, withMs?), formatDuration(ms).
  Packing/layout: packTracks(items) → {tracks, trackCount} (greedy
    first-fit; deterministic under re-ordering — sorted by (start, id)
    internally, results index-aligned to the input; end null = ongoing
    blocks its track; every item occupies >= PACK_MIN_MS so coincident
    instants stack), packVisibleTracks(items, view) → {tracks,
    trackCount} (same packing over only the items intersecting `view` —
    partial overlap counts, out-of-view items get track -1, trackCount
    >= 1 so an empty window collapses to one track; assignment is a pure
    function of the visible set, so sliding over unchanged overlap never
    hops tracks — but membership churn reflows it: the element rows its
    lanes through TrackAllocator instead), class
    TrackAllocator(memoryCap? = TRACK_MEMORY_CAP (2048)) — the STICKY
    stateful variant: assign(items, view) → {tracks, trackCount} with the
    same contract, except a continuously-visible item KEEPS its track, a
    returning item reclaims its remembered one when conflict-free
    (LRU-bounded id → track memory), and new/displaced items take the
    lowest track with no time overlap among this call's visible
    placements — density recovers from the bottom as bursts scroll away,
    visible same-track overlap stays impossible, a fresh allocator's
    first call equals packVisibleTracks, deterministic per call sequence,
    layoutLanes(trackCounts, metrics, trackHeights?) →
    {tops, heights, totalHeight} (per-lane trackHeights override the
    metrics' track height — compact lanes; fractional counts AND heights
    allowed — used for height tweens), trackTop(track, metrics,
    trackHeight?), laneHeight(trackCount, metrics, trackHeight?).
  Auto-fit: demotionOrder(trackCounts) → laneIdx[] (demotion priority:
    track count DESC, ties later-in-display-order first),
    computeAutoFit(trackCounts, metrics, compactTrackHeight, availHeight,
    prevDemotedCount?, hysteresisFrac?) → FitResult {demoted: boolean[],
    count} (demote whole lanes to the compact track height, one at a
    time in demotionOrder, until the stack fits availHeight or all are
    compact; pure and deterministic; demotion is immediate, promotion
    needs FIT_HYSTERESIS_FRAC (0.1) headroom — feed `count` back as
    prevDemotedCount on the next evaluation; the demoted SET re-derives
    from the CURRENT counts, so window slides hand demotion to the
    now-tallest lane; compactTrackHeight clamps to the normal height),
    FIT_HYSTERESIS_FRAC.
  Labels/instants: fitText(text, availPx, charW, minChars?) (verbatim,
    'abc…', or '' — never overflows), ELLIPSIS,
    isInstantWidth(widthPx, threshold?) / INSTANT_THRESHOLD_PX (= 3px —
    below it an interval renders as an instant pip),
    durationWidthPx(startMs, endMs, view, plotWidth) (duration mapped
    through the scale — the translation-invariant width the bar-vs-pip
    decision must use), MIN_BAR_PX (= 2px minimum rendered bar width),
    edgeContinuation(startMs, endMs, view, plotWidth, fadePx) → {left,
    right} (which ends the view CLIPS — the span truly continues
    off-screen past them; exact-edge ends are exempt with half-a-pixel
    slack for the device-pixel view snap, and a side only counts when the
    visible part reaches through fadePx; pass the live edge as endMs for
    ongoing intervals — drives the element's edge shadow).
  Instant clustering: clusterInstants(items, view, plotWidth, joinPx?,
    instantPx?, maxSpanPx?) → {clusters: InstantCluster[], memberOf:
    number[]} (the scale-aware greedy transitive sweep behind the
    element's stacked cluster markers:
    terminal items whose duration maps under instantPx merge while their
    starts sit within joinPx (CLUSTER_JOIN_PX = 12) of a neighbor at
    this scale, up to a cluster width of maxSpanPx
    (CLUSTER_MAX_SPAN_PX = 24) — the cap bounds how far a pip is
    compacted from its true time (half that) and is what keeps a dense
    run a ROW of markers instead of one chained blob at wide zooms;
    clusters have >= 2 members, everything else gets
    memberOf -1; membership depends only on time deltas + scale — pans
    never re-cluster, zooming in splits; deterministic under input
    re-ordering; InstantCluster = {indices, extent} with extent the
    member start range), clusterZoomView(extent, minSpan?, fillFrac?) →
    TimeView (the cluster-click zoom target: extent centered at
    CLUSTER_ZOOM_FILL_FRAC (0.6) fill, floored at minSpan — deep enough
    to split the cluster; coincident members floor at minSpan),
    clusterMarkerTime(extent, view, marginMs) → number | null (marker
    anchor: the extent midpoint, slid along the visible slice when a
    window edge clips the extent — the sticky-label pattern — inset by
    marginMs; null once nothing of the extent is visible).
  Minimap strip: minimapExtent(earliestStart, latestEnd, now,
    exhaustedBefore?, coveredStart?, minSpanMs?) → TimeView | null (the
    strip's data extent: the earliest known start — interval, first
    covered time, or exhausted boundary, whichever is oldest — through
    max(now, latest end); null with no start knowledge; degenerate spans
    pad backward to minSpanMs (60s)), minimapWindowRect(view, extent,
    width, minPx?) → {x0, x1} (the viewport mapped into strip px, CROPPED
    at the strip edges — never slid to a lying position — with
    MINIMAP_MIN_WINDOW_PX (6) enforced around the center before cropping;
    fully-outside views pin a sliver at the nearer edge),
    minimapHitZone(x, rect, hitPx?) → 'left-handle' | 'right-handle' |
    'inside' | 'before' | 'after' (handles win over the middle; zones
    reach MINIMAP_HANDLE_HIT_PX (8) outside the rect but only
    min(hitPx, width/4) inside it, so a narrow window keeps a grabbable
    middle), minimapPan(view, dxPx, extent, width) → TimeView
    (grab-the-middle: constant-span pan by a pixel delta at the extent's
    scale, clamped inside the extent; wider-than-extent windows pin to
    the live end), minimapResize(view, 'left'|'right', xPx, extent,
    width, minSpan?, maxSpan?) → TimeView (drag one window edge to a
    strip x, clamped to the extent and [MIN_SPAN_MS, MAX_SPAN_MS];
    dragging past the other handle CLAMPS at the min span — never flips;
    the min-span floor wins over the extent clamp),
    minimapCenter(view, xPx, extent, width) → TimeView (click outside
    the window: re-center at the clicked time, span preserved,
    extent-clamped). Types: MinimapWindowRect, MinimapZone.
  Hit testing: expandHitRect(rect, minW) (widen instants' hit targets),
    hitTestRects(x, y, rects) (topmost = last; -1 on miss),
    distSqToSegment(px, py, ax, ay, bx, by), hitTestPolyline(px, py, pts,
    tol), connectorRoute(from, to, samples?) (sampled cubic S-curve from
    right-center to left-center; 2-point segment when aligned forward),
    segmentAtTime(segments, intervalStart, intervalEnd, t) →
    SegmentHit {index, kind, start, end} | null (the phase PAINTED at
    time t: last covering array entry — draw order overpaints — with the
    draw clamps applied; half-open [start, end) except t at the
    interval's own end still hits a segment ending there; feeds the
    interval hit's `segment`).
  Category color: hashString(s) (FNV-1a 32-bit), categoryHue(s) (stable
    0..359, golden-ratio spread), categoryJitter(s) (deterministic small
    {dl, dc} tone offsets), categoryColor(hue, {mode 'oklch'|'hsl',
    lightness?, chroma?, alpha?}) → CSS color, dimColor(color) → the
    uniform dim transform (HSV 50% saturation + 50% value, hue/alpha
    untouched; parses #hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla(), oklch();
    unsupported forms pass through unchanged — the element applies it
    to a `dimmed` region's fill/hatching/border, never to label text),
    labelHaloColor(fg) → the label-halo rim color ('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55)'
    under a light fg, 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.55)' under a dark one —
    whichever of black/white contrasts more with the fg itself;
    unparseable fg falls back to the dark rim). The element strokes it
    under every span-surface label so text keeps guaranteed contrast on
    any background at any zoom.
  Styles: DEFAULT_STYLES (the built-in StyleMap described above; the
    dim/queued/hatch/waiting entries set `dimmed: true`).
  Coverage: mergeRanges(ranges), subtractRanges(span, covers),
    historyProbe(view, now, coveredEnd, prefetchFrac?) → TimeRange | null
    (the range loadRange may be asked about: viewport + backward
    prefetch, clamped to now AND the covered end — the forward-edge
    clamp that stops a follow-mode viewport from refiring a request per
    round-trip as "now" advances), class CoverageTracker({minChunkMs?,
    retryMs?}) — addCovered(start, end),
    coveredRanges(), coveredEnd() (end of the newest covered range, null
    when empty), pending(), uncoveredIn(span), nextRequest(view, now)
    (returns the next range to fetch and marks it in flight; one at a
    time, min-chunk widened, null while
    covered/in-flight/retry-gated/exhausted), settle(range, {ok,
    exhausted?}, now?) (success covers + optionally pins exhaustedBefore;
    failure schedules a retry on a FIXED cadence — default 2s, constant
    forever, no growth/cap/give-up), waitingRetry(now) (true while a
    failed load waits out the cadence — frame loops must keep pumping
    while it is), exhaustedBefore.
  Render pacing: RenderTier ('interactive' | 'idle' | 'idle-battery'),
    frameBudgetMs(tier) (0 / IDLE_FRAME_MS ≈ 33.3 / IDLE_BATTERY_FRAME_MS
    = 100), shouldRender(nowTs, lastRenderTs, budgetMs, rafIntervalMs?)
    (rAF frame gate with anti-aliasing slack), INTERACT_GRACE_MS (= 500ms
    of full rate after the last input), clockDrawBudgetMs(view,
    plotWidthCss, dpr, tierBudgetMs) → number (draw budget while the only
    motion is clock-driven: max(tierBudgetMs, span/(plotW*dpr)) — the
    per-device-pixel period, i.e. min(tier fps, device px/sec) in budget
    form; the tier budget is a hard floor so the chart never renders
    faster than the tier pacing, and there is deliberately NO upper cap —
    delivery is the caller's rAF loop skipping frames on an even
    due-time grid, never a timer; degenerate geometry falls back to
    tierBudgetMs).

### ui/dag-view.js
Canvas-painted, pan/zoom directed graph as a <dag-view> custom element.
You hand it nodes and edges; it lays them out in layers, routes the edges,
and owns panning, zooming, hover, selection, search and keyboard
navigation. Re-exports everything from ui/dag-view-math.js, so one import
serves both. No dependencies.

CANVAS, NOT SVG: a few hundred nodes with their edges is a few thousand
SVG elements, and every pan then asks the engine to re-style and re-layout
all of them. Canvas makes a pan one transform plus a redraw of what is on
screen, which is what makes a whole org's repositories usable rather than
merely possible.

WHAT THE LAYOUT COULD NOT HONOUR IS SHOWN, NEVER SWALLOWED. A circular
dependency is drawn dashed in the emphasis colour with its arrow still
pointing the true way; an edge naming a node that does not exist, a
self-loop and a duplicate are dropped and COUNTED. A dismissible notice
strip names all of it, and `info` returns the same facts as data.

  <dag-view id="deps" orientation="TB" empty-text="No dependencies">
    <p>loading graph...</p>   <!-- light DOM: shown until upgrade -->
  </dag-view>

  const el = document.getElementById('deps');
  el.setData({
    nodes: [{id: 'a', label: 'api', sublabel: 'org/api', category: 'svc'}],
    edges: [{from: 'a', to: 'b'}],   // read "b depends on a"
  });

INPUT: drag pans; ctrl/cmd+wheel and pinch zoom; a PLAIN wheel PANS rather
than zooming, so an embedded graph never swallows a page scroll that was
meant for the page. Hovering a node fades everything outside its
dependency neighbourhood; clicking pins that; double-click zooms to the
neighbourhood; the arrow keys walk the graph along its edges once
something is selected, and pan when nothing is. +/- zoom, 0 fits, Escape
clears. The search box HIGHLIGHTS rather than filters, because the edges
are the reason a match matters.

Properties:
  nodes: DagNode[] / edges: DagEdge[] / setData({nodes?, edges?})
  orientation: 'TB' | 'LR'        mirrors the attribute
  styles: DagStyleMap             state -> treatment, merged over DEFAULT_STYLES
  tooltipFor: (hit) => {title?, rows?} | null    null = no tooltip
  colorFor: (node) => string | null             null = derived category hue
  selected: string | null         the selected node's id, settable
  viewport: {x, y, scale}         get/set the pan and zoom
  info: DagInfo                   counts, critical path, crossings, cycles, rejected
  fullscreen: boolean             reflected viewport-fill mode
  fit(pad?)                       fit the whole graph on screen
  focusNode(id, zoom?)            centre + select a node (zoom defaults to current)

Attributes: orientation, no-search, no-toolbar, no-fullscreen-button,
no-minimap, empty-text, fullscreen.

Events (all CustomEvent): `nodeclick` {node, placed}, `edgeclick` {edge,
placed}, `nodehover` {hit|null}, `selectionchange` {node|null},
`layoutchange` (detail is DagInfo), `fullscreenchange` {fullscreen}.

Node states: a `state` string picks a treatment from the style map.
Built-ins are done (solid), blocked (hatched), pending (dashed outline),
missing (dim dashed outline) and failed (stippled). A state with no entry
draws as a plain solid node in its category colour -- a readable node,
never a blank one, so a producer can add a state tomorrow.

Colour is DERIVED: a node's `category` (falling back to its own id) hashes
to a stable hue, so one category is one colour forever and an
uncategorised graph is still multi-coloured rather than one wall of blue.

Level of detail: below scale 0.4 labels stop being drawn; below 0.22 a
node is a plain filled mark. Accessibility: the host is focusable with
role="application", and a selection change is announced through a live
region with its dependency and dependent counts.

Theme via --dag-* custom properties (dag-view.css): --dag-bg (MUST be
opaque -- the canvas is opaque so text keeps subpixel antialiasing), --dag-fg,
--dag-muted, --dag-grid, --dag-hairline, --dag-edge, --dag-accent,
--dag-emphasis, --dag-font, --dag-font-size, --dag-node-radius,
--dag-cat-lightness, --dag-cat-chroma, --dag-gap, --dag-layer-gap.

### ui/dag-view-math.js
The pure half of <dag-view>: the layered (Sugiyama) layout pipeline, the
viewport transform, culling, hit tests and reachability. No DOM, so it
runs and is unit-tested under node. Import it alone to lay a graph out
without rendering one.

The pipeline, each stage exported separately so a consumer can stop after
any of them: buildGraph -> breakCycles -> assignLayers -> insertDummies ->
orderLayers -> assignCoordinates. `layoutDag(nodes, edges, opts?)` is all
of it, returning placed boxes and routed polylines.

DETERMINISM IS A CONTRACT: every tie breaks on the node's index in the
input, never on Map iteration order and never on a random source, so the
same graph draws identically on every machine and every reload. A graph
that reshuffles on refresh cannot be compared to what you saw a minute
ago.

Exports:
  buildGraph(nodes, edges) → DagGraph
    Dense indices, both adjacency directions, and `rejected`: every edge
    naming an unknown node, every self-loop and every duplicate, WITH its
    reason. Nothing is dropped in silence.
  breakCycles(graph) → {reversed, out, in}
    Reverses the back edges a DFS finds, and REPORTS them. A layered
    drawing must break a cycle to draw at all; hiding which edge it cut
    would hide the finding the reader opened the graph for.
  assignLayers(graph, acyclic, {align?}) → {layers, maxLayer, ignoredPins}
    Longest-path layering. A node's `layer` hint can push it DOWN but
    never above one of its own dependencies; an overruled hint is named in
    ignoredPins. align: 'sources' (default) or 'sinks' (bottom-aligned).
  topoOrder(out, n) → number[]
    Kahn order, ties on index. A node left inside a cycle is APPENDED,
    never lost.
  insertDummies(graph, acyclic, layered) → ProperLayering
    Splits every multi-layer edge into per-layer bend points, so a long
    edge occupies real width in each layer it crosses instead of cutting a
    chord across the drawing. Slots are keyed by IDENTITY, not position,
    because the next stage permutes every layer.
  orderLayers(proper, sweeps?) → number
    Weighted-median sweeps plus adjacent transpose. Keeps the best
    arrangement seen, so it can never return a worse one than it started
    with. Returns the crossing count it settled on.
  countCrossings(proper) / crossingsBetween(proper, layer) → number
  assignCoordinates(proper, sizes, opts?) → CoordResult
    Cross-axis placement: pack, then repeatedly pull each slot to the
    median of its neighbours and re-separate. A straight chain comes out
    straight, and no two boxes in a layer ever overlap.
  layoutDag(nodes, edges, opts?) → DagLayout
    {nodes, edges, byId, width, height, orientation, crossings,
    cycleEdges, rejected, ignoredPins}. A reversed edge's `points` still
    run from its TRUE source to its TRUE target, so an arrowhead always
    means what it says. Opts: orientation, gap, layerGap, dummyWidth,
    passes, sweeps, align, sizeOf.
  anchorPoint(placed, orientation, 'in'|'out') → {x, y}
    Mid-point of the facing edge -- an arrowhead at a box centre is one
    nobody can see.
  measureNode(node, opts?) → {w, h}
    Default box size from the label text, clamped between DEFAULT_NODE_MIN_W
    (72) and DEFAULT_NODE_MAX_W (240) so one long title cannot set the
    whole layout.
  Viewport: worldToScreen / screenToWorld / panViewport /
    zoomViewportAt(v, ax, ay, factor, min?, max?) (the world point under
    the anchor does not move) / zoomFactorForWheel(px) /
    fitViewport(rect, vw, vh, pad?) / clampViewport(v, bounds, vw, vh,
    margin?) (a leash, not a fence: it only stops the drawing being
    flicked out of sight) / layoutBounds(layout) / visibleWorldRect.
    MIN_SCALE = 0.05, MAX_SCALE = 4, ZOOM_PX_PER_DOUBLE = 260.
  Culling: rectsOverlap, visibleNodes(layout, rect), visibleEdges(layout, rect).
  Hit tests: hitTestNodes(layout, wx, wy) (topmost wins),
    hitTestEdges(layout, wx, wy, tol) (NEAREST wins, not first), nodeRect.
  neighbourhood(layout, index) → {ancestors, descendants, edges}
    Everything up-stream and down-stream, transitively, following the TRUE
    edge directions including the ones cycle-breaking reversed.
  criticalPathLength(layout) → number   longest dependency chain, in nodes.
  nodeHue(node) → 0..359                category, else the id.

Types: DagNode, DagEdge, DagOrientation, DagGraph, RejectedEdge,
CycleResult, LayerResult, LayerOptions, LayerSlot, ProperLayering,
NodeSize, CoordOptions, SlotPlacement, CoordResult, PlacedNode,
PlacedEdge, DagLayout, DagLayoutOptions, MeasureOptions, DagViewport,
WorldRect, Neighbourhood.

### ui/color.js
Deterministic category colours, the uniform dim transform and the label
halo -- the colour primitives shared by the canvas-painted components
(<timeline-view>, <dag-view>). Pure; no DOM, no clock, no random source.
Re-exported by ui/timeline-view-math.js, so an existing import of these
from there keeps working.

  hashString(s) → uint32              FNV-1a, stable across platforms.
  categoryHue(category) → 0..359      golden-ratio scattered, so similar
                                      strings land far apart. Same string,
                                      same hue, forever.
  categoryJitter(category) → {dl, dc} A second discriminator: tone offsets
                                      (|dl|<=0.05, |dc|<=0.02) so two
                                      categories that hash to nearby hues
                                      still separate.
  categoryColor(hue, opts?) → string  oklch (even perceived lightness
                                      across hues) or an hsl fallback.
                                      Opts: mode, lightness, chroma, alpha.
  dimColor(color) → string            50% saturation, 50% value, hue and
                                      alpha untouched -- one filter over a
                                      whole region, so text-vs-fill
                                      contrast survives. Accepts hex,
                                      rgb(), hsl(), oklch(); anything else
                                      is returned unchanged.
  labelHaloColor(fg) → string         The translucent counter-colour rim
                                      that keeps canvas label text legible
                                      over ANY fill. Dark under a light
                                      fg, light under a dark one.

Types: CategoryColorOptions.

### ui/hit-test.js
Pointer hit-testing primitives for canvas-painted components. A canvas has
no DOM to hit-test against, so every component that paints its own surface
answers "what is under the pointer?" itself. Pure. Re-exported by
ui/timeline-view-math.js.

  expandHitRect(rect, minW) → HitRect   Widen a hairline target around its
                                        centre so it stays clickable.
  hitTestRects(x, y, rects) → index     Topmost (last painted) wins, -1 on
                                        a miss. Edges inclusive.
  distSqToSegment(px, py, ax, ay, bx, by) → number
  hitTestPolyline(px, py, points, tol) → boolean

Coordinates are CSS px in whatever space the caller works in; nothing here
transforms, so a component with a viewport maps the pointer in first.

Types: HitRect.
